callouts.label: Medical Treatment
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents medical treatment.
callouts.description: Healthcare can address withdrawal, cravings, co-occurring conditions, and overall health.
callouts.ap_tip: Evidence-based medication may be part of treatment. Care should be individualized and respectful.

callouts.label: Counseling
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents counseling.
callouts.description: Counseling can build coping, insight, skills, and a plan for difficult moments.
callouts.ap_tip: Different approaches fit different people. Trust and cultural safety matter.

callouts.label: Peer Support
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents peer support.
callouts.description: People with lived experience can offer understanding, hope, and practical wisdom.
callouts.ap_tip: Peer support complements rather than replaces needed clinical care. Groups vary; finding a good fit matters.

callouts.label: Family and Chosen Family
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents family and chosen family.
callouts.description: Supportive relationships can provide stability, encouragement, and accountability.
callouts.ap_tip: Families may need education and support too. Chosen family can be an important source of care.

callouts.label: Culture and Community
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents culture and community.
callouts.description: Cultural identity, ceremony, faith, language, and community can strengthen belonging.
callouts.ap_tip: Recovery should respect the person’s values. Community strengths are health resources.

callouts.label: School and Work
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents school and work.
callouts.description: Flexible, supportive school or work settings can restore routine and purpose.
callouts.ap_tip: Accommodations may reduce barriers. Recovery is compatible with learning and contribution.

callouts.label: Healthy Coping
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents healthy coping.
callouts.description: Sleep, movement, creativity, connection, and other coping skills support wellbeing.
callouts.ap_tip: Skills are practiced, not perfected. A plan can include several options.

callouts.label: Safe Housing
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents safe housing.
callouts.description: Stable housing can make treatment, sleep, safety, and routines more possible.
callouts.ap_tip: Housing is a health condition, not a reward. Community services can help address barriers.

callouts.label: Supportive Policy
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents supportive policy.
callouts.description: Policies affect access, stigma, treatment, housing, school, and employment.
callouts.ap_tip: Recovery is shaped by systems as well as individual choices. Community action can change those systems.

callouts.label: Relapse Response
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents relapse response.
callouts.description: A return to use signals a need to reassess safety and support, not moral failure.
callouts.ap_tip: Overdose risk may rise after reduced tolerance. Respond quickly and revise the care plan.

callouts.label: Renewed Goals
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents renewed goals.
callouts.description: Recovery can reconnect a person with relationships, learning, creativity, and purpose.
callouts.ap_tip: Goals can be small and flexible. The person defines what progress means.

callouts.label: Long-Term Recovery
callouts.hint: Find the scene that best represents long-term recovery.
callouts.description: Recovery can be an ongoing process with changing needs over time.
callouts.ap_tip: Continued support is normal. Hope and realistic planning can coexist.
